title: the runner over every step
line: runnable steps are read fresh before each run, so a step a run's own regeneration drops is never run and one it opens still gets its turn; a SystemExit from a step's own run rolls that step's transaction back and still propagates

steps.say: two steps written by hand on a person, in order
--all, the first step's own run regenerating the plan: it drops the second and opens a third

expect.why: the step read before the regeneration runs
the one it dropped never runs, the one it opened still gets its own turn
the dropped step is really gone

steps.say: a step whose own run raises SystemExit: the transaction rolls back, the exception still propagates

expect.why: a SystemExit from a step's own run still stops the run: it is not silently swallowed
its write does not survive: the transaction rolled back before the exception was re-raised
